newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks end up slightly, await economic data.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks end up slightly, await economic data.

text.p: Thai stocks gained slightly in thin trade on Wednesday as investors bought discounted stocks ahead of key economic data being released by the central bank on Thursday, brokers said.
"Investors bought some large banks. Remarks by the finance minister on increased January exports failed to boost buying sentiment," said Payuha Boonsiri of Nithipat Capital.
The composite SET index advanced 3.61 points to 714.29 on tiny 2.8 billion baht turnover. The SET-50 index rose 0.30 point to 53.22.

Brokers said remarks by Finance Minister Amnuay Viravan before the market resumed afternoon trade failed to boost sentiment as investors opted to wait for key economic indicators from the central bank.
Amnuay said January exports rose 5.1 percent year on year.
A decision by the U.S. Federal Reserve Board to raise its Fed fund rate 25 basis points did not affect Thai stocks, brokers said.

"The Fed's decision to hike its rate has been discounted by investors. Investors are waiting for fresh, positive news before entering the market," said Busaba Kunasirin of Chao Phya Finance and Securities.
Thai Farmers Bank topped the active list, holding steady at 120 baht, National Finance gained 0.25 to 35.50, Siam Cement advanced eight to 636, and United Communication rose one to 170.
